entries.canonical_title: R2E-Gym: Procedural Environments and Hybrid Verifiers for Scaling Open-Weights SWE Agents

claims.paraphrase: The reported hybrid first restricts candidates to the top-n execution-free scores and then adds execution-based generated-test evidence.
claims.section: Section 4, Efficient Inference Time Scaling With Hybrid Verifiers
claims.project_use: direct fixed-hybrid baseline and novelty boundary

claims.paraphrase: The paper reports that many generated tests neither reproduce the bug nor pass the ground-truth patch.
claims.section: Section 4.2, Comparing Execution-Based and Execution-Free Verification
claims.project_use: motivation for explicit evidence-validity and oracle-hardening actions

entries.canonical_title: LEC: Linear Expectation Constraints for Selection-Conditioned Risk Control in Selective Prediction and Routing Systems

claims.paraphrase: LEC uses a held-out calibration set and a linear expectation constraint to control marginal error probability conditional on selection while maximizing retention, and extends the construction to two-model routing.
claims.project_use: direct accepted-set risk and routing-gate baseline; it does not acquire new SWE evidence or model oracle validity

entries.canonical_title: SWE-RM: Execution-free Feedback For Software Engineering Agents

claims.paraphrase: The paper reports its best RL performance and efficiency from a fixed hybrid execution-free and execution-based reward.
claims.section: Section 5.2.2, Execution-Free Feedback Benefits RL Training
claims.project_use: fixed semantic-plus-execution reward baseline; not evidence acquisition

entries.canonical_title: SWE-World: Building Software Engineering Agents in Docker-Free Environments

claims.paraphrase: SWE-World trains transition and reward models from agent-Docker interactions to approximate execution feedback during SFT, RL, and test-time scaling.
claims.project_use: learned-execution-surrogate baseline

claims.paraphrase: The reported transition-model prompts include curator-only gold patch, test patch, and FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS context.
claims.project_use: upper-bound-only classification when those inputs are unavailable live

entries.canonical_title: EGSS: Entropy-guided Stepwise Scaling for Reliable Software Engineering

claims.paraphrase: EGSS uses tool entropy to locate ambiguous trajectory decisions, selectively invokes an auxiliary judge, and augments test evidence.
claims.project_use: adaptive agent-compute and entropy-gating baseline, distinct from post-generation evidence routing

entries.canonical_title: Conformal Selective Prediction with General Risk Control

claims.paraphrase: SCoRE constructs generalized e-values and applies hypothesis-testing procedures to obtain finite-sample trust decisions for user-defined bounded, continuously valued risk among selected positive cases under exchangeability.
claims.project_use: general selected-risk baseline for calibrated terminal gating, not evidence acquisition or fallible-oracle modeling

entries.canonical_title: From SWE-ZERO to SWE-HERO: Execution-free to Execution-based Fine-tuning for Software Engineering Agents

claims.paraphrase: The training recipe is a global two-stage curriculum using roughly 300k execution-free trajectories followed by about 13k execution-based trajectories.
claims.project_use: global curriculum baseline, not candidate-level evidence routing

entries.canonical_title: TwinRouterBench: Fast Static and Live Dynamic Evaluation for Realistic Agentic LLM Routing

claims.paraphrase: TwinRouterBench evaluates step-level selection of the cheapest sufficient model from the exact router-visible prefix.
claims.project_use: direct model-routing baseline; this project routes evidence instead

claims.paraphrase: Its static labels are execution-verified tier estimates under a fixed downgrade-and-cascade protocol, with a dynamic end-to-end track.
claims.project_use: comparison for deterministic offline routing supervision

entries.canonical_title: Conformal Selective Acting: Anytime-Valid Risk Control for RLVR-Trained LLMs

claims.paraphrase: Conformal Selective Acting maintains a Ville-type e-process per threshold to provide an anytime pathwise selective-risk wrapper for an adaptively updated RLVR-trained specialist LLM under its stated predictable-update and monotone-risk conditions.
claims.project_use: online selective-risk gate baseline; it wraps a policy but does not choose SWE evidence modalities or validate their oracles

entries.canonical_title: Not All Errors Are Equal: Consequence-Aware Reasoning Compute Allocation

claims.paraphrase: The method separates predicted error consequence from the marginal success gain of upgrading compute and prioritizes their product.
claims.project_use: consequence-times-marginal-utility compute-allocation baseline

entries.canonical_title: A Joint Finite-Sample Certificate for Adaptive Selective Conformal Risk Control

claims.paraphrase: The certificate simultaneously upper-bounds selected risk and lower-bounds acceptance probability and deployment utility after adaptive threshold selection from a finite grid, using coupled finite-sample confidence bounds.
claims.project_use: joint risk-coverage-utility reporting baseline; it does not acquire candidate-specific evidence or represent invalid task/verifier truth

entries.canonical_title: From Confident Closing to Silent Failure: Characterizing False Success in LLM Agents

claims.paraphrase: Across five judge models and five prompt conditions plus a full-task-specification baseline, the paper reports that no configuration exceeds 0.65 AUROC on tau2-bench false-success detection; on AppWorld API-call traces, GPT-4o peaks at 0.537 AUROC under the checklist condition.
claims.project_use: stress case against terminal self-report or semantic-judge authority, with no assumed transfer from tau2-bench or AppWorld to SWE patch correctness

entries.canonical_title: All Smoke, No Alarm: Oracle Signals in Agent-Authored Test Code

claims.paraphrase: Applying an eight-category syntactic classifier to 86,156 cumulative agent-authored test-file patches, the paper reports that 80.2% contain weak or no explicit oracle signals; two authors independently labeled a stratified 384-patch sample, rather than semantically adjudicating the full population.
claims.section: Sections II-III.A, oracle-signal classification and RQ1 findings
claims.project_use: cheap static oracle-signal feature and corpus-warning baseline, not a candidate-correctness or semantic test-validity label

entries.canonical_title: Bayesian control for coding agents

claims.paraphrase: The controller maintains a posterior belief over candidate correctness and dynamically chooses whether to gather critic evidence, refine the candidate, invoke an expensive verifier, or stop.
claims.project_use: closest direct cost-sensitive sequential evidence-acquisition baseline; Bayesian routing itself is not novel

claims.paraphrase: The paper defines latent correctness by the terminal oracle result, describes that oracle as a deterministic correctness checker, and uses the Podman-based SWE-bench harness as the repository-level oracle; SWE-bench has no separate public-test critic in the study.
claims.section: Sections 3 and 5.2, Task and Environment and Critics and Oracle Verifier
claims.project_use: novelty boundary for separately modeling task truth, candidate truth, and a fallible verifier rather than treating harness success as correctness

claims.paraphrase: The paper reports that Bayesian controllers are most useful when verification is expensive and critics are informative but imperfect, while a near-oracle public-test gate or unconditional verification can dominate in easier or cheaper regimes.
claims.project_use: direct regime and negative-result baseline against any universal execution-free or always-execute policy claim

entries.canonical_title: The Verification Horizon: No Silver Bullet for Coding Agent Rewards

claims.paraphrase: The paper argues that a policy can outpace a verifier, causing reward hacking or signal saturation, and calls for policy-verifier co-evolution while characterizing verification signals by scalability, faithfulness, and robustness.
claims.project_use: closest dynamic-verifier motivation, distinct from per-candidate sequential evidence acquisition and prospective risk control

entries.canonical_title: To Run or Not to Run: Analyzing the Cost-Effectiveness of Code Execution in LLM-Based Program Repair

claims.paraphrase: The study holds each agent scaffold fixed and varies execution access across four paradigms.
claims.project_use: controlled execution-access baseline

claims.paraphrase: The paper reports that 15-34% of validation feedback is environment error and that usable execution benefit is concentrated.
claims.project_use: motivation for explicit environment and evidence-validity outcomes

entries.canonical_title: Dockerless: Environment-Free Program Verifier for Coding Agents

claims.paraphrase: Dockerless receives the issue, reference patch, and candidate patch, then explores the repository to answer generated verification questions.
claims.project_use: curator-context execution-free upper bound rather than a deployable reference-free action

claims.paraphrase: Verifier training pairs are labeled through standard per-repository Docker evaluation with held-out tests.
claims.project_use: evidence that environment-free inference still learns from execution-derived labels

entries.canonical_title: Don't Blame the Large Language Model: How Scaffolding Evolution Shapes Coding Agent Quality

claims.paraphrase: Holding the underlying LLM fixed, the study evaluates 35 sequential Qwen Code releases on 50 stratified SWE-bench Verified tasks and reports no statistically significant resolve-rate improvement, while later releases consume significantly more resources and sometimes more than double token use and tool calls.
claims.section: RQ1, How does agent quality evolve across successive scaffolding releases?
claims.project_use: scaffold-version and cost control, bounded to one scaffold/model and a 50-task benchmark subset

entries.canonical_title: What Makes a Good Bug Report for an AI Agent?

claims.paraphrase: The controlled report-ablation study reports large, model-dependent solve-rate changes when requirements, localization references, report sections, or report structure are removed.
claims.section: Study 2 controlled ablation and cross-study comparison
claims.project_use: separate agent-relative task actionability from task validity and preserve report-quality subgroups

entries.canonical_title: Bug Report Specification Refinement with Trajectory Guidance for Automated Program Repair

claims.paraphrase: TrajSpec discards the trajectory's candidate patch as untrusted, extracts repository-supported hierarchical evidence, generates and reviews a refined report, and reports downstream Pass@1 gains across multiple repair agents.
claims.section: Approach, RQ2-RQ3 results, and threats to validity
claims.project_use: adjacent specification-refinement baseline and motivation for a distinct costed specification-evidence action

entries.canonical_title: SCATE: Learning to Supervise Coding Agents for Cost-Effective Test Generation

claims.paraphrase: SCATE uses static LOC, WMC, and RFC plus runtime coverage and missed-complexity feedback as context for a LinUCB policy choosing DEFAULT, ANALYSIS, or STOP, with a reward that trades coverage and complexity gains against token-dollar cost and assigns STOP zero reward.
claims.section: Sections II-III, approach and contextual-bandit formulation
claims.project_use: closest direct adaptive test-action and cost baseline, distinct from candidate-evidence routing

claims.paraphrase: The evaluation is limited to Defects4J Java classes, with training and evaluation classes originating from the same projects; the authors also identify single-benchmark and language scope, stochasticity, and possible pretraining contamination as validity limits.
claims.project_use: scope boundary against generalizing test-generation routing to cross-repository candidate verification

entries.canonical_title: Benchmarking Large Language Models on Repairing Qiskit Programs using Bugs4Q

claims.paraphrase: Across six pinned Qiskit releases, the paper reports silent case-version invalidity and that 64.1% of observed repair passes occurred on case-version pairs that failed benchmark validation; it also cautions that passing repairs may reflect weak oracles or test overfitting.
claims.section: Abstract, Section III, and threats to validity
claims.project_use: direct evidence that environment identity, task validity, executability, and candidate correctness require separate labels

entries.canonical_title: ReProAgent: Tool-Augmented Multi-Stage Agentic Generation of Bug Reproduction Tests from Issue Reports

claims.paraphrase: ReProAgent decomposes reproduction-test generation into localization, root-cause analysis, assertion-aware planning, and test generation, then executes and refines candidate tests with feedback in a Docker-based sandbox.
claims.project_use: strong targeted-execution and generated-reproduction-test action baseline

claims.paraphrase: Using fail-on-buggy and pass-on-patched FP Rate, the paper reports 58.43% and 70.30% reproduction rates on two SWT-bench subsets and an average generation cost of $0.14 per instance with its primary backbone.
claims.project_use: measured-cost baseline whose generated-test oracle still requires independent validity adjudication

entries.canonical_title: How Far Are We from Detecting Flaky Tests? On the Limits of Code-Based Detection

claims.paraphrase: The reported code-only detectors lose their apparent advantage under project-disjoint, rerun-confirmed evaluation, and 58% of 86 flaky end-to-end cases could not be causally attributed from test code plus CI logs without further runtime evidence.
claims.project_use: direct boundary on execution-free sufficiency and motivation for candidate-specific runtime acquisition

entries.canonical_title: Failure as a Process: An Anatomy of CLI Coding Agent Trajectories

claims.paraphrase: The study retrospectively labels decisive-error, lock-in, and observability times from complete trajectories, separately evaluates an outcome-blind prefix monitor, and reports a median decisive-error onset at step 7 with a short intervention window before lock-in.
claims.project_use: rollout-time intervention motivation plus a strict warning not to expose retrospective failure labels to the live policy

entries.canonical_title: Writing Bug Reports for Software Repair Agents: What Information Matters Most?

claims.paraphrase: The controlled content manipulation reports that removing localization and suggested-fix cues together reduces repair success in the pooled model and in two of three per-model analyses, while effects vary across models and report contexts.
claims.project_use: model actionability separately from validity and test specification clarification as an evidence intervention
